To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

shear-enhanced adsorption can be observed in a homopolymeric chain in a small region of the parameter space, when the dissociation rate is low, the association rate is moderate and the catch bond parameter is close to the slip bond limit.
shear-induced adsorption of a collapsed homopolymer can be achieved in a limited range of bond parameters and that the effect is most pronounced for a catch bond.

the adsorption of a collapsed homopolymer can be enhanced by shear flow in a small range in parameter space when the surface-monomyer bond is close to the transition between slip bonds and catch bonds and that the shear-induced enhancement of adsorption can be described by an effective catch bond potential.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the adsorption of a collapsed homopolymer in shear flow onto a planar surface.
the effect of shear flow on the adsorption of a polymer onto a smooth surface.
the adsorption behavior of a homopolymer in shear flow on a planar smooth substrate, where the surface-monomers interact via a two-state stochastic bond model.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the adsorption state diagram is determined by the competition between the shear-induced detachment of surface-monomer bonds and the shear-induced stretching of surface-monomers.

shear-induced adsorption of a globule can occur for surface-monomer bonds with catch-bond characteristics, and for a sufficiently large range of parameters of the bond kinetics.

shear-induced adsorption is possible only when the surface catch bond parameter is near the transition from slip to catch bond.
